unit.why: A single anecdote: R. Moshe Leib of Sasov, hungry at a nobleman's house while ransoming a captive, overcomes his craving for a dish by recalling Shabbat Nishmat, and his disciple of Zidichov draws a teaching from it.

stories.start_quote: פעם אחת הי' אצל שר אחד
stories.summary_en: While at a nobleman's house to ransom a captive and still fasting, R. Moshe Leib of Sasov was seized by craving at the smell of a costly dish but overcame it by recalling the delight of Shabbat Nishmat. He told this to his disciple R. Zvi Hirsh of Zidichov, who commented that each tzaddik has his own world, found in a different part of the prayer.
